title: Metaheuristic Optimization for Multi-AGV Path Planning in Search and Rescue Missions
abstract: This paper addresses optimizing multi-Autonomous Ground Vehicle (AGV) coordination in autonomous ground search and rescue missions, focusing on enhancing exploration efficiency through collaborative path planning. By modeling the environment as a 2D grid and leveraging optimization algorithms, the aim is to maximize area coverage while minimizing exploration time. The optimization problem is formulated based on travel distance and the number of explored grid cells. Simulated annealing (SA), Genetic algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Algorithm (PSO) and Artificial Protozoa Optimizer (APO) are applied to generate optimized paths for multiple AGVs, ensuring efficient task distribution. The performance of each algorithm is evaluated based on the overall objective function and computational time. The results demonstrate the framework’s capability to improve exploration efficiency and path allocation, making it a suitable approach for AGV coordination in large-scale environments.

title: Metaheuristic Optimization for Vehicle Routing and V2G Scheduling in Electrical Vehicle Fleet Network
abstract: The paper investigates the Vehicle Routing and Charging/Discharging Scheduling Problem for an electric vehicle fleet with Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology for a given network. Moreover, it compares different algorithms to maximize the revenue generated by V2G through the charging and discharging of electric vehicles, while ensuring they reach their destination by a given deadline. In order to reduce the high complexity of the problem, four different metaheuristic algorithms are introduced: Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Discrete Grey Wolf Optimizer (DGWO), and Shuffled Frog Leaping Algorithm (SFLA). The performance of the implemented metaheuristic algorithms is also examined through multiple experiments with different tuning parameter. The performance of each algorithm has been found to vary significantly. The research also provides insights in effective configuration for the Vehicle Routing and Charging/Discharging Scheduling Problem for Vehicle-to-Grid with a focus on profit maximization.

title: Optimizing Multi-UAV Cooperative Task Assignment for Fire Extinguishing Missions
abstract: Forest fires represent a growing global threat, with millions of hectares lost annually due to their rapid spread and devastating impact on ecosystems, biodiversity, and human settlements. The increasing frequency and intensity of such disasters motivate the need for intelligent and automated solutions capable of responding swiftly and efficiently. In this context, cooperative task assignment for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) emerges as a promising approach to enhance aerial firefighting and surveillance operations. However, this remains a challenging problem due to its combinatorial nature, multiple conflicting objectives, and operational constraints. This work formulates the UAV–task assignment problem as a multi-objective optimization model that maximizes task value while minimizing UAV losses and the number of deployed UAVs. To solve this problem, four meta-heuristic algorithms are investigated: Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Discrete Grey Wolf Optimizer (DGWO), and Binary Firefly Algorithm (BFF). Each method is adapted to operate directly on binary assignment matrices with appropriate constraint-handling mechanisms. Simulation results demonstrate that the Binary Firefly Algorithm (BFF) achieves the best overall performance in terms of solution quality and consistency, while Simulated Annealing (SA) exhibits the fastest convergence speed among the compared methods. Overall, the evaluated algorithms effectively produce high-quality feasible task allocations, though runtime trade-offs must be considered for time-critical wildfire deployment scenarios.

title: Comparative Analysis of Meta-Heuristic Algorithms for Multi-Robot Search and Rescue
abstract: We present a comparative analysis of four metaheuristic optimization algorithms applied to the Multi-Robot Search and Rescue (MRSAR) problem: Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), and Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO). The objective of the algorithms was to minimize the cost function of the rescue operation, made up of the robot’s travel distance and the adherence to the rescue time window. Experimental results indicate that the Genetic Algorithm (GA) achieved the best convergence and final solution quality (Cost approximately 103), followed closely by Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO).

title: Metaheuristic-Based Navigation Optimization for Heterogeneous Autonomous Vehicle Fleets
abstract: The Heterogeneous Fleet Vehicle Routing Problem (HFVRP) represents a complex combinatorial optimization challenge with significant real-world applications in logistics and supply chain management. This paper presents a comparative study of four metaheuristic algorithms-Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), and Teaching-Learning Based Optimization (TLBO)-applied to the HFVRP. The problem is modeled with strict hard constraints on vehicle capacity and maximum travel distance, prohibiting any infeasible solutions during the search process. A ”Best Insertion” heuristic is implemented to generate feasible initial solutions. The algorithms are evaluated on a set of seven test cases of increasing complexity, ranging from simple 4-customer scenarios to a largescale 60-customer challenge. Performance is analyzed based on solution quality (final cost), execution time, and convergence behavior. Results indicate that while population-based methods like ACO and TLBO offer robust search capabilities, the singlepoint Simulated Annealing algorithm demonstrates superior efficiency and solution quality for the specific constraints and scale of the tested instances.

title: Weather-Adaptive Task Allocation for Vehicle Fleets in Disaster Relief Operations: A Multi-Scenario Optimization Framework
abstract: Multi-cooperative Vehicle Fleets have been the subject of many research papers and rigorous tests over the years. In this paper we aim to implement a novel multi-level optimization architecture, that optimizes both path and task allocation through the use of state-of-the-art optimization techniques and algorithms on Disaster relief operations. This architecture takes into account Weather Conditions, like Wildfires, Blizzards, Floods, and many more. Due to the severity and sensitivity of the context, it is very crucial that the applied Optimization techniques take into account these weather conditions and their effects on a vehicle fleets’ Speed, fuel consumption, distance traveled, task allocation, chosen path and the overall success of the operation. The main algorithms covered in this paper are Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Discrete Grey Wolf and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC).

title: Optimizing Multi-Robot Delivery in Smart Hotels: A Multi-Objective Metaheuristic Approach
abstract: This paper addresses the multi-robot task allocation problem in multi-floor indoor service environments by evaluating and comparing several metaheuristic algorithms, including Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), and Multi-Objective Artificial Bee Colony (MOABC). The problem is formulated as a multi-objective optimization that simultaneously minimizes total travel distance, completion time, and workload imbalance among heterogeneous robots operating across multiple floors. Through multiple independent runs, the results demonstrate that MOABC consistently achieves superior solution quality with the lowest variability, while GA provides a favorable trade-off between optimality and computational efficiency. SA delivers near-instantaneous convergence, whereas ACO exhibits limited scalability. All evaluated approaches yield a substantial reduction in workload variance, confirming the effectiveness of population-based metaheuristics for multi-objective task allocation in service robotics.

title: Meta-heuristic Adaptive Exploration Strategy Through Routing Optimization
abstract: Efficient exploration of unknown environments by multi-robot teams requires a delicate balance between coverage maximization and the maintenance of communication connectivity. While various metaheuristic approaches such as Genetic Algorithms (GA), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), Simulated Annealing (SA), and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) have been applied to this problem, no single algorithm dominates across all environmental conditions. For connectivity-constrained scenarios with sparse initial robot configurations, constructive methods like ACO often excel, whereas perturbative methods like SA may offer superior computational efficiency in simpler scenarios. We introduce MAESTRO, a framework that integrates a learned router (Random Forest) to dynamically select the optimal planner based on extracted map features and connectivity/topology statistics. Our evaluation, performed on a dataset of 1,836 test scenarios, demonstrates that this adaptive approach achieves a classification accuracy of 94.99% in selecting the optimal solver. We further conduct a sensitivity analysis on GA population sizing, proving that adaptive routing outperforms even hyperparametertuned static solvers. Crucially, the system exhibits a fail-safe routing behavior: in our testing, it achieved zero critical errors, correctly avoiding the lightweight solver (SA) for complex instances requiring robust optimization (ACO), thereby minimizing mission failure risk while reducing computational overhead by approximately 34%.

title: Hybrid Energy System Planning: Optimizing Solar and Wind Power for Maximum Efficiency and Cost Reduction
abstract: This project optimizes a hybrid renewable energy system with photovoltaic (PV) panels and wind turbines, aiming to minimize costs and maximize energy output. Advanced optimization techniques, including Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO), and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), are used to find near-optimal solutions within practical constraints. The decision variables include the number of PV panels and wind turbines, while the objective functions minimize costs and maximize energy output. Each algorithm offers unique advantages, with SA balancing global and local searches, GA emphasizing population diversity, GWO leveraging cooperative behavior, and ABC enhancing exploration and exploitation. Case studies reveal trade-offs between solar and wind configurations, demonstrating the potential of hybrid systems for cost-effective, energy-efficient solutions.

title: Route to Clean Cities: Waste Collection Optimization with UGVs
abstract: Efficient waste collection is crucial to effective urban management, with farreaching implications for environmental sustainability, public health, and overall quality of life in cities. As urban populations continue to grow, the demand for optimized waste management systems becomes increasingly critical. This study addresses the challenge of designing efficient waste collection routes using metaheuristic optimization techniques. Specifically, four different algorithms are employed to minimize route lengths, reduce operational costs, and improve the scalability of waste collection systems. These algorithms are rigorously evaluated in a variety of test configurations that simulate real-world scenarios. The results of the experiments reveal the strengths and limitations of each algorithm, providing valuable insights into their applicability for real-world waste management systems.

title: Development and Evaluation of Various Optimization Techniques for Multi-Robot Task Allocation and Routing in Warehouse Settings
abstract: The coordination of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) in modern warehouses presents a complex multiobjective optimization problem involving task allocation, routing efficiency, collision avoidance, and energy management. As warehouse systems scale, many existing optimization approaches become computationally expensive or require extensive parameter tuning. This paper proposes a Teaching–LearningBased Optimization (TLBO) framework for multi-robot task allocation and routing in structured warehouse environments. The proposed method integrates task assignment, robot routing, battery-aware operation, and collision avoidance within a unified optimization formulation. The TLBO algorithm is evaluated through simulation in three warehouse instances of increasing complexity. Its performance is compared with Genetic Algorithm (GA), Simulated Annealing (SA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) under identical modeling assumptions. Experimental results demonstrate that TLBO achieves stable convergence behavior and consistently produces feasible collision-free solutions across all warehouse scenarios while eliminating the need for algorithm-specific parameter tuning. The results indicate that TLBO provides a robust and scalable optimization framework for energy-aware multi-robot warehouse coordination.

title: Reinforcement Learning Based Optimization Technique for Road-Side-Units (RSUs) Placement along a Highway
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Reinforcement Learning (RL) optimization technique for Road-Side-Units (RSUs) placement along a highway. With RSUs playing a crucial role in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), the optimization of RSU placement is crucial for efficient communication. This research aims to optimize the cost of the RSU deployment along the highway as well as to minimize the delay in communication between vehicles. For the purpose of this research, two different deterministic RL algorithms were tested, the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithms. Both algorithms are a modelfree off-policy Actor-Critic algorithms with deterministic actions. The algorithms’ performance was then compared to three different famous Meta-Heuristic algorithms, Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Discrete Particle Swarm Optimization (DPSO). Training results and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) show a faster run time for the deterministic RL algorithms for the same number of iterations as the Meta-Heuristic algorithms. KPIs also showcase the better solution cost achieved by the RL agents for the specific optimization problem.

title: Coordinated Defense via Multiagent Optimization in Distributed Target-Attacker-Defender Games
abstract: In modern autonomous aerial defense, the cooperative interception of hostile threats presents a complex, dynamic optimization challenge. This paper addresses the multiagent Target-Attacker-Defender (TAD) game, where a team of defending Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) must coordinate to protect a high-value asset from non-cooperative attackers. We formulate the TAD problem as a constrained multi-objective optimization task, balancing formation cohesion, interception efficiency, and target guarding. While recent literature explores learning-based approaches, this work rigorously evaluates the efficacy of nature-inspired metaheuristic algorithms for realtime decision-making. We implement and compare four distinct solvers: Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), and the Bat Algorithm (BAT). Extensive simulations across balanced, aggressive, and defensive tactical scenarios reveal significant trade-offs between solution stability and optimality. Our results demonstrate that while population-based methods like GA and GWO offer superior consistency with low variance (std dev < 0.04), the Bat Algorithm achieves the highest peak performance, locating ”super-optimal” defensive configurations with a mean fitness improvement of approximately 13% over standard evolutionary methods. This study provides a unified framework for comparative analysis and offers critical insights into selecting optimization strategies for swarm-based aerial defense systems.

title: Metaheuristic Optimization for Efficient Food Production Scheduling
abstract: In this paper, we explore multiple metaheuristic optimization techniques for multi-cooperative production scheduling in the food industry. Our approach aims to minimize production costs by optimizing energy consumption, labor deployment, and raw material utilization while adhering to practical constraints such as demand satisfaction, production line exclusivity, where each line can produce only one product at a time, and line changeover time. Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Social Spider Optimization (SSO) algorithms are implemented and evaluated on this problem. We validate the performance of each algorithm using two case studies, each representing contrasting scenarios in terms of demand and power consumption. Finally, all the results were analyzed and compared, highlighting the PSO algorithm’s efficiency in generating cost-effective schedules compared to other algorithms. However, it came to be very computationally expensive. This study also demonstrates the potential of SSO in addressing complex production scheduling problems in manufacturing, as the results are similar to PSO with a slight difference.

title: Scaling Multi-Robot Search and Rescue: A Comparative Study of Metaheuristic Exploration Methods
abstract: Autonomous multi-robot systems provide a safer alternative to human responders in hazardous disaster environments. This work evaluates a multi-objective grid-based exploration strategy that maximizes coverage while minimizing redundancy, exploration time, and constraint violations. Four metaheuristic algorithms—Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Aquila Optimization Algorithm (AOA)—are assessed across three environments of increasing complexity. While AOA performs best in small-scale settings, its effectiveness declines as the search space grows. SA and PSO achieve competitive coverage in medium scenarios but struggle with refinement and penalty avoidance at larger scales. Overall, GA exhibits the strongest scalability, maintaining a superior balance between coverage and constraints in complex environments, indicating that populationbased evolutionary strategies are more robust for large-scale disaster response.

title: Multi-UAV Trajectory Planning and Task Allocation for Disaster Rescue Operations
abstract: This paper presents a constrained multi-UAV routing framework for disaster rescue missions that incorporates load-dependent endurance coupling and time-window constraints within a unified optimization model. Segment cost is dynamically linked to remaining payload, capturing realistic energy–mass interactions during flight. The objective integrates travel cost, UAV activation cost, temporal penalties, and utilization efficiency rewards. Two solution strategies are proposed: a Discrete Teaching–Learning-Based Optimization with Local Search (DTLBO-II-LS), featuring class-based learning and embedded local search operators for robust low-variance combinatorial routing, and a policy-gradient Reinforcement Learning formulation (REINFORCE) that generates adaptive routing policies through episodic sampling without predefined neighborhood operators. Both are benchmarked against three classical metaheuristics: Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) under a unified framework. Across 10- and 20-node scenarios, DTLBO-II-LS attains the lowest variance (4.64 over 20 runs) and outperforms GA by approximately 2% in larger instances, demonstrating superior robustness and convergence stability, while SA achieves the best single-run cost (−950.41). REINFORCE produces competitive feasible solutions and demonstrates adaptive behavior, though variability increases with problem scale. These results demonstrate that structured discrete metaheuristics (SA, GA, DTLBO-II-LS) offer superior solution quality and robustness for time-critical UAV disaster response, while learning-based routing (REINFORCE) provides a flexible, operator-free alternative whose scalability can be improved through enhanced policy parameterization and reward design. The two paradigms thus represent complementary directions: metaheuristics for deployment-ready optimization and RL for adaptive long-term learning.

title: Multi-Agent Racing Trajectory Optimization with Tire Wear Awareness: A Comparison of Reinforcement Learning and Metaheuristic Methods
abstract: This paper implements multiple algorithms to achieve racing line optimization with respect to tire wear and lap time minimization on a 3 DOF model-based vehicle and Pacejka tire model. We evaluated metaheuristic algorithms such as Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic algorithms (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) and compared their results to Machine Learning approaches such as Reinforcement Learning (PPO). The primary testing ground was the Autodromo Nazionale Monza which acted as benchmark to obtained results. We evaluated each method across three key performance indicators lap time, tire degradation, and computational latency. While population-based metaheuristics achieved better lap time results (76.17s), they are computationally expensive (> 866.11s runtime). However, the RL agent demonstrated a reduction in computational time (14.13s), suggesting real-time generation with only a marginal 3.5% deficit in lap time performance (78.87s). These results highlight that while meta-heuristic algorithms achieve better overall results their extreme computational need makes the RL results better.

title: Optimization of Multi-AGV Scheduling for Airport Baggage Handling
abstract: Efficient coordination of Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) is critical for mitigating the multi-billion dollar operational losses associated with airport baggage mishandling. This paper presents a multi-objective optimization framework for AGV scheduling, formulated as a Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (VRPTW) on a bidirectional linear topology. We evaluate five distinct optimization paradigms: three established meta-heuristics (Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO)), a proposed Hybrid Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm, and a Reinforcement Learning (RL) (Q-Learning) approach. The Hybrid ABC approach utilizes discrete neighborhood operators for routing and continuous vector updates for temporal scheduling, while the Q-Learning agent offers sub-second responsiveness for dynamic environments. Experiments across three operational scenarios (standard, small, and a high-pressure First Come First Serve (FCFS) instance) demonstrate that the Hybrid ABC algorithm achieves the highest optimality, improving upon the traditional FCFS method by 61% and reducing fleet requirements by 40% in the Standard instance. Conversely, the Q-Learning agent provides the highest execution efficiency, establishing a clear trade-off between planning quality and real-time responsiveness.

title: Advancing Sustainable Energy: Analyzing Stochastic Algorithms and Q-Learning for Wind Farm Layout Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the optimization of wind farm layouts, a critical aspect of enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of wind energy production. We delve into various optimization techniques, including Simulated Annealing, Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Moth Flame Optimization, and Deep Q-Learning. Each optimization technique is explored through a series of case studies, where different configurations and parameters are applied to assess their effectiveness in optimizing wind farm layouts. These techniques are evaluated based on criteria such as computational complexity, optimality of solutions, and repeatability of results. The paper’s findings offer insightful comparisons and analyses of each technique, providing an understanding of their respective strengths and limitations in the context of wind farm layout optimization.

title: Autonomous Intersection Management Platform (AIMP): Metaheuristic Optimization for Traffic Scheduling
abstract: Autonomous Intersection Management (AIM) enables signal-free coordination of Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAVs) to improve traffic efficiency while maintaining safety. This paper presents a priority-aware AIM framework formulated as a mixed discrete–continuous optimization problem using a conflict-point abstraction. Multiple metaheuristic algorithms are compared for vehicle ordering and speed optimization. A Hybrid ACO–PSO method is proposed to separately optimize the discrete passing sequence and continuous vehicle speeds. Experimental results demonstrate improved convergence stability, robustness, and computational efficiency, making the hybrid approach a balanced solution for priorityaware intersection scheduling.

title: Performance Evaluation of Meta-Heuristic Algorithms for Multi-Robot Task Allocation
abstract: Multi-Robot Task Allocation (MRTA) is a nondeterministic polynomial-time (NP)-hard optimization problem that requires assigning tasks to multiple robots while minimizing travel cost, maximizing task coverage, and maintaining workload balance. This paper evaluates four meta-heuristic algorithms, Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), and the Bee Algorithm (BA), for solving MRTA using a unified multi-objective formulation based on distance minimization, task maximization, and Jain's Fairness Index. Each method is tested under multiple parameter settings to analyze convergence behavior, solution quality, and computational efficiency. Simulation results show that the Genetic Algorithm achieves the best overall performance, providing the highest task coverage and fastest convergence while preserving balanced task distribution among robots. Although BA and GWO offer stable and fair solutions and SA produces energy-efficient routes, GA consistently outperforms the other methods in both solution quality and runtime. These results highlight GA as the most suitable choice for scalable and efficient MRTA applications.
